text: sealed at 0538db5c7d4a52bc4f7712061763a6efc9e3ff72; seal-time probe script metric=26 target=0 measuring=true

seal.statement: Every registered invariant cites a contract the impact-contract registry knows: each of the 26 citations the derived harness model reports as unbound either receives a registration in test/shards/impact-contracts.json with exactly one witness test, or a ruled-out finding retiring the citation from architecture/contracts/invariants.json, so that no invariant remains that nobody can witness and the harness model's unbound count reaches zero by derivation.

text: Inventory of the 26 unbound citations (derived from the probe on 94cfca8a0, not typed; contractIdOf = basename of contractRef minus .md; an invariant binds when the registry knows that id AND the contract has at least one src/ owner). Four groups. (A) 12 citations whose contractRef is a closure-ledger entry or an epic AND which already carry liveEvidence.evidence.test, an existing red-on-violation witness: CL-041/CL-042/CL-040 (test/closure/CL-04x.repro.test.js, owners src/raft/liferaft.js + in-memory-log-adapter.js), CL-038 (test/rebalancer/cl-038-source-removed-handoff-terminates.test.js, src/rebalancer/priority-publication-leader-safety.js), CL-035 (test/control-plane/cl-035-voter-ready-row-seed.test.js), CL-033 (cl-033-planning-projection-memo.test.js, src/control-plane/control-plane-readiness-publication-planning-snapshot.js), CL-034 (cl-034-planning-snapshot-merge-memo.test.js, ...planning-resolution.js), CL-001 (test/control-plane/active-node-projection.test.js, src/control-plane/active-node-projection.js), golden-capability-gold-plating (test/rebalancer/failed-authoritative-read-admission-verdict.test.js), publication-readiness-churn-liveness-closure x3 (publication-readiness-churn-liveness.test.js twice, control-plane-read-authority-token.test.js once - one contract id, three invariants: a contract id carries ONE witness under the constraint, so the two invariants sharing publication-readiness-churn-liveness.test.js bind through it and readiness-owner-read-non-amplifying needs its own contract id or a ruled-out finding). (B) 11 core-system-logic invariants (architecture_owner, Alloy model architecture/models/alloy/core-system-logic.als plus statechart; witnessed today only by test/scripts/model-contract-tools.test.js, which checks the model files exist and parse - not red on a violated invariant): one registration whose witness is the Alloy run if a test can be made to fail on a violated assertion, else ruled-out per invariant as architecture-level with no src/ owner (the binding rule needs one). (C) readiness-handoff-liveness x2 (startup_runtime_handoff_owner, TLA models/readiness-handoff/ReadinessHandoff.tla, no liveEvidence; owner under src/bootstrap/shared/startup-runtime-handoff-owner*): a red-on-violation witness to write, or a ruled-out finding. (D) rolling-restart-rebalancer-handoff x1 (bounded-owner-reentry, operation_workflow_owner, src/rebalancer/operation-workflow-owner-ports.js per the contract doc's ownerBoundaryMap): as C. Constraint check: retire-or-register-never-relabel forbids pointing an epic-cited invariant at an unrelated registered contract; registering the ledger/epic basename itself as the contract id is what the binding rule reads, so (A) registers those ids as they stand and re-points nothing. Decide per group in the first attempt.

Group A registered: ten contract ids added to test/shards/impact-contracts.json, each with exactly one witness (the invariant's own liveEvidence.evidence.test, already red on violation) and the owner modules that witness imports: CL-041, CL-040, CL-042 (src/raft/liferaft.js + in-memory-log-adapter.js; test/closure/CL-04x.repro.test.js), CL-038 (priority-publication-leader-safety + -shared; cl-038-source-removed-handoff-terminates), CL-035 (replica-handler + priority-publication-safety-topology; cl-035-voter-ready-row-seed), CL-033 (readiness-publication-planning-snapshot; cl-033-planning-projection-memo), CL-034 (planning-resolution + readiness-service; cl-034-planning-snapshot-merge-memo), CL-001 (active-node-projection + projection-readiness-state; active-node-projection.test), golden-capability-gold-plating (replica-status; failed-authoritative-read-admission-verdict.test), publication-readiness-churn-liveness-closure (readiness-service + planning-snapshot + owner-key-reconcile-queue; publication-readiness-churn-liveness.test - the witness two of its three invariants name; the third, readiness-owner-read-non-amplifying, keeps its own liveEvidence witness control-plane-read-authority-token.test.js, which the registry already carries under readiness-versioned-planning-liveness). Ids are the citations' own basenames; nothing re-pointed. Probe 26 -> 14; audit:impact-contracts PASS (30 contracts); owner-interaction-model contract 5/5 with the new hosts; change-selection taxonomy 7/7 and the change-selection family green.

State after group A (probe 14): every remaining citation lacks a runtime red-on-violation witness, and each needs an owner decision rather than more registration. (B) the 11 core-system-logic invariants are architecture_owner invariants with NO src/ owner by design; they are witnessed at the MODEL level - 7 as Alloy assertions (check ... for 6 in architecture/models/alloy/core-system-logic.als), all 11 in the statechart, 3 in decision-tables/bounded-retry-exit-routing.json, 4 in traces/core-owner-trace-examples.json - through model:alloy, model:statecharts, model:decision-tables and check-owner-traces (test/scripts/check-owner-traces.test.js is red on a hidden trace violation). The binding rule (registry contract with a src/ owner) cannot bind them without inventing owners; retiring them from invariants.json would sever the model tooling that validates against their ids. Two honest options: (B1) widen the derived model with a second binding class, model-witnessed, an invariant whose modelRef names a model the model:contracts chain checks, counted separately from unbound and never as hosted - a rule change to owner-interaction-model.js under this quest's derived-not-typed constraint; (B2) retire per invariant with ruled-out findings and accept the model-tooling breakage as a follow-up. (C) readiness-handoff-liveness x2: the owner exists (StartupRuntimeHandoffOwner, src/bootstrap/node-joining-owner-construction.js, bootstrap-service.js, node-joining-service-shared.js; contract doc architecture/contracts/readiness-handoff-liveness.md) but the only tests naming it are harness readiness-normalization and timeout-formatter tests, not witnesses of 'ready requires a serviceable canonical leader at a fresh owner epoch' or 'the startup handoff is eventually terminal'; a witness must be written over the real owner (readiness cannot become active with SQL/query transport unserviceable; a handoff that never receives its evidence still terminates), or the two are retired. (D) bounded-owner-reentry: the owner path is the operation-workflow recovery observation (src/rebalancer/operation-workflow-recovery-observation.js, COORDINATOR_CREATED_CACHE_REENTRY state table; contract ownerBoundaryMap names operation-workflow-owner-ports.js); the existing operation-workflow-progress-event-driven-reentry.test.js asserts that re-entry ARMS bounded verification, not that a reconciled-but-unpublished node is deferred back to pending a bounded number of times - the invariant's predicate; the abstract model test (test/model/active-gate) proves boundedness on AbstractGate, not on the owner. A runtime witness must be written (drive the real owner through repeated defer-eligible observations and assert the count is capped), or the citation retired. Recommendation: B1 for the eleven (model-witnessed is what they are), written witnesses for C and D (three tests, real owners, one per invariant... C has two invariants and one contract id, so one contract witness that fails on either).

Group A registered (26 -> 14). The remaining 14 need an owner judgment before any further move: (B) the eleven core-system-logic invariants are model-witnessed with no src/ owner - widen the derived model with a model-witnessed binding class (B1, recommended) or retire them (B2, breaks model tooling); (C) readiness-handoff-liveness x2 and (D) bounded-owner-reentry have real owners but no red-on-violation witness - write one witness per contract over the real owner (recommended) or retire.

Owner decision (2026-09-12). (1) B1, narrowly: a model-witnessed binding class under four conditions - (i) the pointer resolves to a NAMED assertion the chain actually runs (an Alloy assert/check, a statechart property, a decision-table rule), never to 'appears in the statechart'; the derived model validates it the way it validates seam pointers, dangling or unnamed turns the receipt red; (ii) the model:alloy / model:statecharts / model:decision-tables / check-owner-traces chain must be in a gate that runs (test:static or the change-selection family) - if it is not, getting it into the gate is the first commit of this attempt, before any binding; (iii) subject test: the class is only for invariants whose subject is the architecture itself (ownership topology, state-machine shape, decision structure); any of the eleven that claims runtime behaviour (timing, liveness, what a node does under load) goes to group C/D for a real-owner witness - classify all eleven by subject in a finding, one or two are expected to fail; (iv) the receipt reports three counts, never one: hosted, model-witnessed, unbound - the class keeps the number visible. (2) Write the witnesses, do not retire: one witness per contract id (three tests - readiness-handoff-liveness gets a witness that fails on either of its two predicates counted as one contract? NO: three tests, one per contract id... readiness-handoff-liveness x2 share one id, bounded-owner-reentry one id; the owner asked for three tests so the registration rule stays uniform - one per invariant, registered under the contract id with the contract's witness being the one that fails on either); red-on-violation by mutating the owner's predicate, not the test; 'eventually terminal' and 'at most N' under the injected clock, N read from the owner's configuration; a predicate that cannot be made red by mutating the owner is not an owner invariant and is ruled out.

Subject classification of the eleven core-system-logic invariants (condition iii). ARCHITECTURE (subject is the topology, state-machine shape or decision structure; declared subject: architecture in invariants.json): single-semantic-owner (ownership topology; Alloy assertion SingleSemanticOwner), normalized-state-only (state shape at the ingress boundary; NormalizedStateOnly), owner-outcome-before-observer (the shape of the owner->observer flow - borderline, an ordering claim, kept as architecture because it constrains where a projection may sit in the flow, not when; OwnerOutcomeBeforeObserver + the forbidden trace observer-projects-before-owner-outcome), readers-do-not-repair-authority (ownership: readers never write authority; ReadersDoNotRepairAuthority + trace), durable-transition-has-recoverable-wake (structural: every durable transition carries a wake; DurableTransitionHasRecoverableWake - its modelRef pointed at the statechart, which names no per-invariant property, and now points at the Alloy model where its assertion is declared and checked: a pointer correction, the same assertion the chain already ran), single-canonical-outcome (decision structure: one rule per input combination, all nine rules), non-shrinking-evidence-blocks-local-retry (rule non-shrinking-repeated-local-retry-blocks), deferred-followup-has-recoverable-wake (rule deferred-followup-available-budget-wakes). RUNTIME - fail the subject test and go to group C/D for a real-owner witness: degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness (what the readiness owner does with degraded evidence), stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness (what readiness does with a stale projection epoch across a handoff - CL-012 territory), phase-owner-handoff-completes (a liveness claim about bootstrap/join/recovery phase owners completing their handoff; also modelled only in the statechart, which names no check). Three, not the one or two expected. The statechart is not a witness for anything: it lists invariants by id and statement but names no property per invariant, so 'appears in the statechart' resolves to nothing - the model reports it as a problem when a declared subject points there.

B1 landed in the working tree (14 -> 6). (1) First commit 94baafff4, before any binding: architecture/models/** and architecture/contracts/invariants.json were INERT to change selection, so a model edit ran no checker locally (repository-health ran model:contracts only after the push); they are now a governed source (source-architecture-models -> architecture-governance, inert rule narrowed) and the architecture-model-chain contract selects test/scripts/model-contract-tools.test.js, check-owner-traces.test.js and model-invariants.test.js for any edit under them (verified: selectChangedTests on the Alloy file and the registry lists exactly those three). (2) The class, in test/distributed/harness/owner-interaction-model.js: an invariant declared subject: architecture in invariants.json is MODEL-WITNESSED only when its modelRef resolves to a NAMED check the chain runs, resolved with the chain's own validators (validateAlloyModel/validateDecisionTable/validateTraceSuite reject -> problem): an Alloy assertion that is both declared (assert X) and checked (check X) for the invariant's invariantRefs entry; a decision-table rule whose invariantRefs names it; a forbidden owner trace that declares the violation AND whose evaluator (collectTraceViolations) produces it. A statechart names no property per invariant and resolves to nothing. A declared subject whose pointer dangles is a problem: the receipt test fails and the probe exits non-zero even at unbound 0. Precedence: registry-hosted first, then model-witnessed, else unbound. (3) Three counts everywhere: invariantBindings returns bound/modelWitnessed/unbound/problems; the probe prints 'counts: hosted=18 model-witnessed=8 unbound=6' plus every MODEL-WITNESSED, UNBOUND and PROBLEM line, metric still the unbound count; the harness contract test asserts the three-way partition, no problems, and that every model-witnessed invariant declares the subject and names an existing model. (4) Eight declared architecture (see the classification finding); durable-transition-has-recoverable-wake's modelRef corrected from the statechart to the Alloy model where its assertion is checked. Verification: owner-interaction-model contract, model-invariants, model-contract-tools, check-owner-traces and change-selection-taxonomy tests 41/41; the formation quest's receipt harness 5/5; guideline checkers 0 new. Remaining six are group C/D: real-owner witnesses to write.

Group C/D witness investigation (next sitting starts here; probe 6: bounded-owner-reentry, degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness, phase-owner-handoff-completes, stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness, ready-requires-serviceable-canonical-leader, startup-handoff-eventually-terminal). Facts: (1) readiness-handoff-liveness.md's own safetyInvariants list ready-requires-serviceable-canonical-leader, stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness AND durable-transition-has-recoverable-wake, its livenessExpectations startup-handoff-eventually-terminal; runtime bindings src/bootstrap/owners/startup-runtime-handoff-owner.js (StartupRuntimeHandoffOwner: activateControlPlaneBackgroundWriters with a 1000 ms retry timer, activateDistributedTransactionRecovery with NOT_STARTED/PENDING/COMPLETED/FAILED state), src/bootstrap/shared/startup-sql-runtime-handoff.js (attachSqlRuntimeToStartupOwner, activateSteadyStateRuntimeHandoff, buildStartupRuntimeHandoffSnapshot), src/bootstrap/shared/local-query-transport-readiness.js (getLocalQueryTransportReadiness / isLocalQueryTransportReady / waitForLocalQueryTransportReadiness with backoff), and src/control-plane/read-model-contract.js for the observer side; consumers of the evidence: join-readiness-snapshot-methods.js, bootstrap-service-seed-workflow.js, node-joining-backfill-merge-and-status.js, bootstrap-readiness-dependency-probes.js. stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness cites core-system-logic but the handoff contract claims it as its own safety invariant with a real owner - registering it under readiness-handoff-liveness needs its contractRef re-pointed to the doc that actually claims it (related, not unrelated; record as a decision when done). (2) bounded-owner-reentry: the contract binds runtime to src/rebalancer/operation-workflow-owner-ports.js (priority_recovery_event_driven_wait retry wake), models it in models/active-gate/ActiveGate.tla (DeferReentry) and test/model/active-gate/model.js (AbstractGate.deferReentry with allowUnboundedReentry); the real owner code has NO explicit re-entry bound constant (grep maxReentries/REENTRY_LIMIT/reentryCount over src: nothing) - the runtime re-entry classification lives in operation-workflow-recovery-observation.js (COORDINATOR_CREATED_CACHE_REENTRY state table) and operation-workflow-owner-priority-recovery-reentry.js; the witness must find where the deferral count is capped (or the retry budget that caps it: decision table bounded-retry-exit-routing retryBudget available/exhausted), read N from there, and drive the real owner under the injected clock; if no cap exists in the owner, the predicate cannot be made red by mutating the owner and is ruled out per the decision. (3) degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness and phase-owner-handoff-completes cite core-system-logic; registering core-system-logic as a contract would host the eight architecture invariants through it - the model's precedence (hosted before model-witnessed) would let a registered core-system-logic swallow them; if the runtime two are registered there, precedence must become model-first for declared-architecture subjects, or the two are re-pointed to the owner contract that claims them (readiness owner: control_plane_readiness_owner / readiness_gating 'cannot upgrade stale or degraded evidence' is named in readiness-handoff-liveness's ownerBoundaryMap). Witness plan, one file per contract id, one test per invariant, red by mutating the owner's predicate: readiness-handoff-liveness (4 tests over StartupRuntimeHandoffOwner + the two serviceability modules: not active while SQL or query transport unserviceable; not promoted from a stale owner epoch; deferred handoff terminal under the injected clock - ready/blocked/escalated; durable transition carries a wake) and rolling-restart-rebalancer-handoff (deferral cap N from the owner).

Group C, first witness (test/bootstrap/readiness-handoff-liveness-witness.test.js, not yet registered - the contract's single witness file is registered only when every invariant it claims has its test there). startup-handoff-eventually-terminal: the owner's deferred handoff (waitForLocalQueryTransportReadiness over a REAL unstarted MessageRouter, whose query/data-plane transport is honestly unavailable) terminates blocked within the bound the owner itself reports on every retry (onRetry {attempt, maxAttempts}; N read from the owner at run time, never typed), every deferral on the injected sleep (none on the wall clock), attempts counted monotonically, and the terminal outcome is typed (progressContract: blockingDependency local_query_transport, nextAction wait_for_local_query_transport, a wakeSource, retryAfterMs). Red-on-violation by mutating the OWNER: with the owner's bound removed (unbounded loop) the witness fails - 'owner slept 25 times past its own bound of 24: the startup handoff is not terminal' - and the owner is restored byte-identical (git diff empty). Next: ready-requires-serviceable-canonical-leader over the same owner path - registerSeedNodeWithControlPlane (bootstrap-service-control-plane-runtime-methods.js) waits for the system service leaders (SeedCacheHydrationPhase.waitForSystemServiceLeadersInCache over the leader-readiness gate for NODES/NODE_ENDPOINTS/SERVICES) and then awaitLocalQueryTransportReadinessForReadySignal BEFORE the node row and the first heartbeat are written; the witness hosts the real method with satisfied leaders and an unserviceable transport and asserts the typed not-ready rejection and an empty nodes table; then stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness and durable-transition-has-recoverable-wake over the same contract, then group D.

Group C, second witness in the same file and the registration. ready-requires-serviceable-canonical-leader: the REAL seed registration owner (createBootstrapServiceControlPlaneRuntimeMethods, production prototype inherited; registerSeedNodeWithControlPlane) hosted over real owners - the node's CDC owner and gateway, the real HeartbeatService, the real SeedCacheHydrationPhase over the seed's delegates, the SQL-engine seam - with canonical leaders for the seed's three required-write tables as rows applied through the cache owner's own apply (partition row with leader node + active leader partition service; the seam knows no partitions table, so the replication leg lands them rather than widening the seam) and a REAL unstarted MessageRouter whose query/data-plane transport is honestly unavailable. The owner passes the leaders wait, defers on the injected clock, and refuses with its own typed code ROUTER_QUERY_TRANSPORT_NOT_READY (progressContract.blockingDependency local_query_transport); the nodes table stays empty. Red-on-violation by mutating the OWNER: with the transport gate line removed from registerSeedNodeWithControlPlane the witness fails (the node row registers / the code is not the gate's), owner restored byte-identical (git diff empty). Registered: readiness-handoff-liveness with owners bootstrap-service-control-plane-runtime-methods.js, owners/startup-runtime-handoff-owner.js, shared/startup-sql-runtime-handoff.js, shared/local-query-transport-readiness.js and the single witness test/bootstrap/readiness-handoff-liveness-witness.test.js; both invariants citing it now bind (probe 6 -> 4: hosted 20, model-witnessed 8, unbound 4: bounded-owner-reentry, degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness, phase-owner-handoff-completes, stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness). audit:impact-contracts PASS; harness model contract + taxonomy green.

Pointers for the last four (probe 4; next sitting starts here). (1) stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness: the owner predicate is the projection readiness decision (src/control-plane/projection-readiness-decision.js): PROJECTION_READINESS_INTERNAL_BLOCKERS and _REPAIR_BLOCKERS both refuse when evidence.projectionRevision.stale === true with reason PROJECTION_REVISION_STALE - a witness drives the exported decision with a stale revision under the internal and repair lanes and asserts not-ready + that reason, red when the blocker entry is removed from the owner; it must also cover the handoff boundary the contract names (readiness-handoff-liveness lists it as its own safety invariant): the readiness owner's stored-snapshot path (control-plane-readiness-snapshot-store.js '::stale=' key, CL-012 window) is where a stale projection could promote across a publication apply. Binding: its contractRef is core-system-logic.md; the handoff contract claims it verbatim, so re-pointing the citation to readiness-handoff-liveness.md is a related-contract correction to record as a decision, not a relabel to an unrelated contract. (2) degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness: owner surfaces are RUNTIME_AUTHORITY_PUBLICATION_STATE.DEGRADED (control-plane-readiness-runtime-authority-methods.js:57, readiness-planning-publication-contract.js:285, eligibility-snapshot.js:184) and PUBLICATION_ACTIVE_GATE_HANDOFF_STATE.DEGRADED (publication-active-gate-handoff-contract-decision.js:114,208,223) - the witness asserts that a DEGRADED runtime-authority publication state cannot produce a promoted readiness/admission outcome in those decisions, red when the DEGRADED branch is folded into the healthy one. (3) phase-owner-handoff-completes: bootstrap-service.js:409 constructs the StartupRuntimeHandoffOwner and :496 the seed phase owners (createSeedPhaseOwners); activateSteadyStateRuntimeHandoff (startup-sql-runtime-handoff.js:202) is the transfer; the witness must show a phase owner's responsibility (background writers, transaction recovery, latency topology) is held by the steady-state owner after handoff and that the phase owner is no longer reachable/active - find the release point in bootstrap-service-seed-workflow.js / seed-delegates stopAndClearControlPlaneServices. (4) bounded-owner-reentry: the owner's bound is the per-operation retry budget - ports.readRetryBudget(operation) -> buildOperationWorkflowOwnerPortRetryBudget(owner, operation) (operation-workflow-owner-ports.js:869), evidence field retryBudget with OPERATION_WORKFLOW_RETRY_BUDGET_STATE (available/exhausted) and reason RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (operation-lifecycle.js:247); the decision table bounded-retry-exit-routing routes exhausted budgets to block/escalate. The witness drives the real OperationWorkflowOwner through repeated defer-eligible evidence for one reconciled-but-unpublished node under the injected clock and asserts the deferrals stop at the budget the port reports (N read from the port), red when the budget check is removed.

Binding precedence corrected in the derived model: an invariant declared subject: architecture binds ONLY through its model check - it never falls back to a host, so a contract registered under the same citation (core-system-logic will carry the runtime invariants that share the document) cannot swallow the eight architecture invariants into 'hosted'; a dangling model pointer stays a problem. Counts unchanged (hosted 20, model-witnessed 8, unbound 4); harness model contract 5/5. Existing witness found for stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness: test/control-plane/projection-readiness-contract.test.js 'ProjectionReadiness blocks stale local projection revision by lane' drives the owner's projection readiness decision with localProjectionRevision < requiredProjectionRevision and asserts internal and serve lanes closed with reason PROJECTION_REVISION_STALE - red when the stale blocker leaves PROJECTION_READINESS_INTERNAL_BLOCKERS in projection-readiness-decision.js. It witnesses the projection owner's half; the handoff-boundary half (CL-012 stored-snapshot window) is the readiness owner's.

Two of the three core-system-logic runtime witnesses, in test/control-plane/core-system-logic-runtime-witness.test.js (not yet registered: the third, phase-owner-handoff-completes, is still to write; the file becomes the contract's single witness only when all three are in it). stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness: the owner's projection readiness decision (buildProjectionReadinessContract) with every dimension healthy and the publication acknowledged promotes at the published revision (control) and, with the local projection one revision behind, promotes NO lane - internal, repair and serve all closed, ready false, reason PROJECTION_REVISION_STALE; red when the stale blocker is removed from PROJECTION_READINESS_INTERNAL_BLOCKERS/_REPAIR_BLOCKERS in projection-readiness-decision.js. degraded-evidence-never-upgrades-readiness: the owner's active-node projection in convergence mode (resolveActiveNodeViews, allowControlPlaneRecoveryEligibleProjection) with an unhealthy cluster-member dimension projects the node on ESTABLISHING runtime authority (control) and refuses RETAINED and UNAVAILABLE runtime authority - not projected, not a runtime-authority inclusion, excluded by readiness and explained in the diagnostics; red when resolveProjectionReadinessRuntimeAuthorityProjection accepts RETAINED. Both owners restored byte-identical after the mutation runs.

Owner decision (2026-09-12) on stale-projection: do NOT re-point; trim the handoff contract. An invariant is cited by exactly one contract - the one whose witness goes red when the predicate is mutated; stale-projection's witness is the core-system-logic runtime file, so the citation stays there. readiness-handoff-liveness claiming it verbatim while its witnesses test terminal-ness and the serviceable-leader gate is a contract claiming what its witness does not check - the drift mechanism in miniature. Edit the contract's claim text to reference the invariant as a dependency rather than assert it, then make the rule mechanical in the derived model: every invariant id a contract's text names must be either the contract's own bound citation or marked as a reference; a bare claim of someone else's invariant is a problem, same class as a dangling pointer - registry as a function, not a relation. Confirmed as-is: three of eleven failing the subject test; owner-outcome-before-observer stays architecture on one condition - it binds through a forbidden owner-trace (structural), and the day a runtime test asserts the same ordering it moves; durable-transition's modelRef correction. Last four: bounded-owner-reentry's N comes through ports.readRetryBudget at test time, red when the owner defers past its own budget; phase-owner-handoff-completes runs the real seed workflow under the injected clock, red by skipping activateSteadyStateRuntimeHandoff. Done when the probe reads 0 with three non-zero counts.

Stale-projection decision applied. (1) readiness-handoff-liveness.md trimmed: its safetyInvariants now claim only ready-requires-serviceable-canonical-leader (plus the liveness expectation startup-handoff-eventually-terminal); stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness and durable-transition-has-recoverable-wake remain in systemTheory.invariantRefs as dependencies and the prose Invariants section says so - the contract references them, it no longer asserts them. model:contract-records still validates the record (invariantRefs must be registered ids, which they are). (2) The rule is mechanical in the derived model: contractClaimProblems reads every architecture/contracts/*.md system-contract block and reports, as a problem of the dangling-pointer class, any safetyInvariants/livenessExpectations id that is a registered invariant cited by a different contract; problems fail the harness receipt test and the probe. Census before the trim: the handoff contract was the only foreign claimer (two ids); unregistered contract-local ids (active-gate, rolling-restart, quest-lifecycle) are outside this rule and stay with the system-contract validator. Mutation check: re-adding the stale-projection claim to the handoff contract makes the probe print 'PROBLEM architecture/contracts/readiness-handoff-liveness.md claims stale-projection-never-promotes-readiness, which is cited by architecture/contracts/core-system-logic.md'; doc restored. owner-interaction-model, model-contract-tools, check-owner-traces and model-invariants tests 34/34; counts hosted 20 / model-witnessed 8 / unbound 4 unchanged.

Third core-system-logic runtime witness and the registration (probe 4 -> 1). phase-owner-handoff-completes: the REAL seed workflow methods (createBootstrapServiceSeedWorkflowMethods, production prototype inherited; completeSuccessfulBootstrap) hosted over the real StartupRuntimeHandoffOwner whose steady-state owners are the real LeaseService and HeartbeatService - initialized over the node's real CDC owner and gateway, their interval/timeout functions injected so every periodic arm is recorded on the injected clock and none fires on the wall clock - a real NodeLifecycleStateMachine and a real BootstrapNodeReadyRebalanceOwner. Before completion the handoff owner holds nothing (control); completing the phase issues the transfer (activation promise present), the phase reads COMPLETE, hasActiveControlPlaneBackgroundWriters() holds, lease and heartbeat owners are RUNNING, their periodic work armed on the injected timers. Red-on-violation by mutating the OWNER: with activateSteadyStateRuntimeHandoff removed from completeSuccessfulBootstrap the witness fails; owner restored byte-identical.
